title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A fake cryptocurrency trading app used AI to generate false account balances and investment returns, deceiving a retired Georgia couple into transferring nearly $800,000. The scam began with an unsolicited WhatsApp message and proceeded through a social engineering technique: allowing small withdrawals to build trust before requesting larger transfers. The fraud succeeded because the fake app displayed realistic information that appeared genuine to the user.

The failure was in the mobile application itself, which presented fabricated financial data as fact. No human verification step intercepted the transfers before they were sent. The app operated as a complete impersonation of a legitimate trading platform, combining fake website design with AI-generated false account information.

It is not established how the AI system was trained, whether the scammers built or purchased it, or what technical safeguards might have prevented the impersonation. Police confirmed the money is unlikely to be recovered.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest in cryptocurrency through a mobile trading app, gradually building his trust by allowing small withdrawals. However, the app was fake, using artificial intelligence technology to create a false display of his account balance and investment returns. When Dunaway tried to withdraw a larger amount, he discovered the fraud and contacted police.

The couple, Jerry and Mindy Dunaway, are now warning others about the sophisticated tactics scammers use to manipulate victims. Gwinnett County police confirmed that while the trading app appeared real, scammers had created a fake website that showed false investment information on the screen. Investigators say victims in these cases rarely recover their money. The Dunaways are working with local police and their children have started a GoFundMe page to help them cover living expenses.
